premises.text: Couples lack an everyday way to address relationship challenges; many find therapy ineffective and there has been no digital solution that tracks relationship health
premises.evidence_span: 11 to 18 percent of people that go to therapy find it to be not effective. There is no digital solution

premises.text: Metric-driven onboarding plus AI check-ins, alerts, icebreakers, and activities improve communication, trust, intimacy, and conflict between sessions and in daily life
premises.evidence_span: LifeCouple is a platform that allows couples to address relationship challenges in a way that's suitable for their everyday life

premises.text: Go-to-market complements therapy and Employment Assistance Programs rather than replacing them, unlocking workplace productivity lost to relationship distress
premises.evidence_span: we have built a partnership because we complement therapy. We do not say that therapy is going to be replaced by technology

value.text: Keep relationships healthy by monitoring and intervening like a Fitbit for the heart
value.evidence_span: LifeCouple is a Fitbit for your heart

causal_links.evidence_span: without a good relationship, our lives could somewhat be meaningless
This platform was built to keep a relationship healthy
13 billion dollars is lost of unproductivity because of people divorced or in an unhappy marriage

notes: Four relationship areas, icebreakers, digital gifts, and therapist treatment-plan workflow folded into one everyday relationship-health mechanism (rule 7). CAC/traction figures excluded. Anti-template justified.
